_doc: CPO-approved review routing (governance G3, ruled 2026-06-12). PROTECTED file:
changing who reviews what is a governance event (CPO-approved task with
protected_override). The commit gate computes the REQUIRED reviewer set for a
diff from these path patterns (fnmatch); 'always' reviewers run on every
substantive commit. Commits whose staged paths ALL match 'artifact_only'
patterns are exempt from review (bookkeeping: handover, review files,
escalation log) — EXCEPT any path in 'artifact_only_never' (contract.md
authorizes scope, so a contract change is never exempt; F10/#409).
'hash_exclude_paths' = bookkeeping artifacts excluded from the review
diff_sha256, so the hash covers code + contract.md; CI recomputes
`git diff base...HEAD` over the same exclusion to bind review.md to the PR
(F11/#409). contract.md is NOT excluded — it is hashed, because scope_paths
and acceptance_criteria carry authority and must not move after review.
The two EVIDENCE artifacts ARE excluded (CPO 2026-08-01): they carry
evidence, not authority, and while they were hashed, correcting a typo in
one voided every reviewer's PASS and forced a fresh round. #370 spent
rounds 6-12 on that loop and found nothing a visitor would see.
'review_exclude_paths' = what a reviewer does NOT read (CPO 2026-08-01).
Reviewers judge code and contract.md, never the review's own paperwork.
Consumed by `git_discipline.py --review-patch`, which is how
review_input.patch must be generated. Measured on #370 before this: 839
lines of code inside a 38,932-line reviewed diff, 96% of it the patch file
re-embedding its own previous contents.
LISTED FILE BY FILE, never as the `.claude/task/` directory. TWO files there
carry AUTHORITY and must reach the reviewers: contract.md (scope_paths and
acceptance_criteria) and escalations.log (the durable record of CPO rulings
that protected_override cites). 'Does the claimed ruling actually exist' is a
check that has fired. The rest are notes ABOUT the work and are hidden.
Git pathspecs cannot re-include a path once excluded, so the directory form
silently hid the contract — a test caught it, and cto-reviewer then caught
escalations.log being hidden for the same reason.
`test_every_task_artifact_is_classified` fails when a new file appears in
.claude/task/ that is neither excluded here nor one of those two, so the list
cannot decay as artifacts are added.
JSON not YAML so the stdlib-only hooks can parse it.
Dormant-but-undefined reviewers (activate with their surface): ui-expert
(site_v2 templates/components, when #366/#368 build), data-journalist
(generated narratives, when GAP-03 builds), legal-counsel (crest/logo/photo
asset policy, when site asset work starts).
bi-analyst-reviewer routes to ALL of site_v2/src/** — the BUILT frontend —
as well as the specs (CPO ruling, AskUserQuestion 2026-07-22: 'Yes,
everything under site_v2/src'). The binding rule (docs/wireframes/00_overview.md,
'the whole point') says a block may reference only fields that exist in
today's exported data and that anything missing is never silently drawn — and
that reviewer's first hunt item IS that rule. It was routed to the wireframe
DOCUMENTS only, so the fake planned on 2026-07-22 — two real metrics typed
into a committed sample so a page looked finished while the pipeline could
not feed it — drew [cto-reviewer, scope-auditor], neither of which checks
whether a displayed field exists.
ONE pattern, not a directory list, and that is deliberate: the first attempt
enumerated pages/components/data and MISSED src/lib/metricRows.ts, which
holds the CPO-locked 16-row display contract. A fake needs a row there AND a
key in the sample, so routing the sample alone caught half of a two-file
change. src/lib/format.ts (the no-naked-percentage and null-as-dash rules)
and src/lib/bars.ts (the direction-to-green encoding) were missed too. The
gap was found by enumerating `git ls-files site_v2` — the first attempt was
'verified' against two paths that did not exist because they were files the
builder intended to create. Enumerate the real tree, never the imagined one.
`.claude/agents/**` routes to cto-reviewer (CPO ruling 2026-06-12): a change
to a reviewer definition must be gate-required to get platform review, not
left to only the always-on scope-auditor. The opus-on-guards rule then
overrides that cto review to opus (see docs/working_agreement.md §2).
`.claude/commands/**` is PROTECTED + routed to cto-reviewer (CPO ruling
2026-06-14): a custom slash command can embed shell, so a command file is
governed like a hook — protected-path edit (needs protected_override) +
platform review + opus floor.
`.mcp.json` + `.cursor/mcp.json` are PROTECTED + routed to cto-reviewer (CPO
ruling 2026-06-18): an MCP-server config auto-launches a command every
session — the same command-class as .claude/commands/. Protected-path edit
(protected_override) + platform review + opus floor. .claude/settings.json
(which can carry an mcpServers block) is already PROTECTED.
=== THE CTO SPLIT (CPO ruling 2026-07-31, #868) ===
The CPO's finding, unprompted: 'We have a CTO role that is pulled in every
review process. That's ridiculous.' Measured: cto-reviewer was required on
28% of the last 150 commits, and 48 distinct tracked files matched BOTH
site_v2/** (cto) and site_v2/src/** (bi-analyst), so a CTO reviewed Astro
markup. site_v2/** was its single largest trigger. Root cause: routing has
ONE activation type — file path — and applied it to every role regardless of
what the role is for. Path activation is right for a role that OWNS code and
wrong for an executive that should rule on a PROPERTY of the change.
So: platform-reviewer takes the territory and the line review; cto-reviewer
keeps the authority and loses the broad globs. Measured after: cto 12%,
platform 24%, 10% requiring both. Zero tracked site_v2/src/** files require
either — pinned by a test, because that overlap is what motivated the split.
TWO ROLES ON ONE PATTERN = ONE KEY WITH BOTH NAMES. `paths` is a JSON object,
so json.load silently keeps only the LAST of two identical keys and one
reviewer requirement would vanish with no signal. Nothing in either consumer
detects it. A test now asserts every pattern string appears exactly once in
the raw file text. Found by the pre-CPO plan challenge, not in review.
GUARD PATHS: platform-reviewer joins cto-reviewer on exactly TWO of the eight
— .claude/hooks/** and .github/workflows/** — and the docs must say TWO. The
CTO rules on authority (is protected_override present, is this a new
mechanism, may this guard weaken); platform reviews the implementation (does
it fail open, do the tests cover it, is it re-run safe). Both carry the opus
floor on those two. The other six go to cto-reviewer ALONE plus the always-on
scope-auditor.
This was churned once and the churn is worth recording. Review round 1 caught
three documents claiming BOTH reviewers on all EIGHT guard paths while routing
gave platform two. There were two ways to fix that: widen the rows, or correct
the prose. Round 2 widened the rows to six, and review round 2 correctly
failed it — two opus specialists where one ran before is a RECURRING COST, and
cost is CPO-class, so the cheap fix (correct the prose) was the right one and
the rows are back to two. Do not widen them without a cost approval quoted in
decisions_taken. A doc/row mismatch is fixed by editing whichever side is
wrong, and the wrong side is almost always the prose.
Platform is deliberately absent from .claude/agents/** — a reviewer brief is a
prompt, not machinery, so none of its hunt items apply and its verdict would
be a rubber stamp, which is worse than absent. On that path the CTO is the
whole specialist guard against a builder weakening its own adversary.
KNOWN HOLE, stated rather than left implicit (platform-reviewer, round 2). The
question 'does a test pin this changed behaviour' is platform's hunt item, and
platform is not routed to .claude/agents/** or to this file. For the `paths`
rows the hole is closed by machinery: test_every_routing_pattern_is_pinned_by
_the_test_above forces any pattern change to also edit tests/**, which routes
platform in. That mitigation does NOT exist for the `always` array or for an
agent brief. So on a diff that removes scope-auditor from `always`, or edits a
brief, no required specialist is asked whether a test pins it — only the CTO on
authority and the always-on auditor on scope. Accepted for now; closing it
means either routing platform to these paths (a cost the CPO must approve) or
pinning the `always` array in a test the way the patterns are pinned.
The first draft gave platform the fail-open/fail-closed item at sonnet and
kept the CTO at opus on authority alone; the pre-CPO challenge showed that
hollows out the very depth the opus pin exists for, since the G3 commit-gate
bypasses WERE fail-open and hook-test-coverage findings. Hunt item 4
therefore stayed with the CTO.
site_v2 BUILD CONFIG IS ENUMERATED BY NAME, not globbed, and site_v2/** is
gone. fnmatch's `*` crosses `/`, so `site_v2/*.json` would also match
site_v2/src/data/*.json and re-create the overlap this split removes. Only
two directory globs are used (integrations, scripts) and both were verified
against `git ls-files site_v2` to have ZERO collision with site_v2/src/.
All 11 tracked non-src files are covered, site_v2/.gitignore included: a
path that is covered today does not lose coverage in a split.
`*requirements*.txt` REPLACES `requirements*.txt` — a deliberate correction,
not a widening. fnmatch full-string-matches, so the old pattern anchored at
the start of the path and ingestion/api_football/requirements.txt never
reached the dependency threshold at all. The new pattern matches exactly two
tracked files, verified. A dependency is a dependency wherever it is declared.
seo-expert-reviewer is STILL NOT ROUTED. Approved in principle on 2026-07-31
but not commissioned; it remains its own governance event. It fires on
nothing today. Do not read the split as having routed it.
